title: AnimationNodeTransition cancels ongoing cross-fade when requested with a new transition
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.6.2-stable ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7600 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21025.10016) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 62.95 GiB memory ### Issue description When I have a transition node in my blend tree with an xfade time greater than zero, I notice something unexpected. When transitioning from animation A to B, The animation is blended correctly, but when transitioning from A to B, and during the transition back to A, the blended animation snaps to B before transitioning back to A. This happens even when - unchecking 'Reset' on the inputs - transitioning to another input (for example C). I would expect the transition to blend between a 'current' state and the final state. This is my animation tree: This is the AnimationNodeTransition: I have added a capsule in my scene with two animations: - one where it moves to the left and back - one where it moves to the right and back. In this example I flip between animations using the AnimationNodeTransition every 0.5 seconds: crossfade is not interrupted and snapping does not occur: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01b8acfb-bb87-43f1-bcf7-1b492ef7ff9d In this example I flip between animations using the AnimationNodeTransition every 0.3 seconds: crossfade is interrupted and snapping occurs: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a8c5b30-48c3-4e2f-a7e1-a0a9e8aa58d1 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add a capsule 2. Add an animation player animating said capsule 3. Add an animation tree 4. Add an AnimationNodeTransition with a crossfade 5. During the crossfade of the transition, request another transition 6. Notice how the animation is first fully finished before crossfading again instead of blending between the current state and the newly requested animation ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [transition-node-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29798707/transition-node-mrp.zip)
